Associated topic groups

Topic groups can belong to several code communities. Profiles include each message once within a community, but communities overlap. Neutral and unmapped emotions are reported separately. The 11 categories are a composition, not a validated positive/negative score.

How the two maps compare

The fixed map uses weighted Leiden on the completed tension network. Its groups are displayed with coloured boundaries and readable community buttons. The animated map progressively counts topic-group incidence, updates the same Jaccard weights, and moves nodes using attraction and repulsion. Its colours come from a separate live modularity optimisation. It does not steer nodes toward the fixed groups.

At full ingestion, the two views have the same supported edge weights. Their positions and community memberships need not be identical. The live algorithm is a transparent multilevel Louvain-style optimiser; the fixed analysis uses Leiden. The displayed ARI compares their memberships on linked reference codes.

The enriched animation uses the final archive's BY-qualified edge set as an eligibility gate, then reveals its weights gradually. It is a replay of the qualified graph, not a sequence of early-data significance tests. Shuffled topic order is a robustness exercise, not historical time.
